proposed.title: Iron Fist S2#5
proposed.text: Colleen and Misty find Walker guarding Joy, and Walker fights Colleen and nearly cuts her throat before Misty arrests her and they take her back to the dojo.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: A spy who turns out to be Walker. Nearly kills Colleen before Misty arrests her.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: Danny's girlfriend, whom Walker fights and nearly kills before her arrest.

changes.evidence: In 'Heart of the Dragon' (Iron Fist S2#5) Colleen and Misty go to Joy's apartment, Walker attacks them, overpowers Colleen and is about to drive her machete into Colleen's throat when Misty holds her at gunpoint and cuffs her; they take Walker and Joy to the dojo. The stages stop at S2#4 with Colleen only suspecting her.

proposed.title: Iron Fist S1#2
proposed.text: Ward offers Colleen money to testify against Danny, and she turns him down after talking to Danny in the hospital.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: Joy's brother, who tries to pay Colleen to testify against Danny.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: A dojo owner who refuses Ward's money to testify against Danny.

changes.evidence: The connection starts well before S1#13: in 'Shadow Hawk Takes Flight' (Iron Fist S1#2) Harold sends Ward to offer Colleen money for testimony against Danny and she refuses; in S1#3 Ward's security men attack her. Ward only allies with Colleen and Danny in S1#13.

proposed.title: Luke Cage S1#4
proposed.text: Shades and Darius, known as Comanche, are fellow inmates at Seagate who do the guard Rackham's dirty work together, running his prison fights and beating Carl Lucas.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: A fellow Seagate inmate who does Rackham's dirty work with Comanche.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: A fellow Seagate inmate who does Rackham's dirty work with Shades.

changes.evidence: In the Seagate flashbacks of 'Step in the Arena' (Luke Cage S1#4) Comanche and Shades are shown together as Rackham's enforcers: they ambush Lucas in his cell, bring him to the fight ring and later beat him with steel weapons together. The first stage is only at Luke Cage S2.

now.title: Luke Cage S1#3
now.text: Domingo Colon is an old friend turned rival of Cottonmouth's in Harlem's drug trade.
now.on_a_card_about_b: An old friend turned rival in Harlem's drug trade.
now.on_b_card_about_a: An old friend turned rival in Harlem's drug trade.

proposed.text: Domingo Colon, who was buying Hammer guns from Cottonmouth, declares war on him after the deal goes wrong and Cottonmouth refuses him a refund.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: A rival gang boss who declares war over a failed gun deal.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: A crime boss who refuses Colon a refund on a failed gun deal.

changes.evidence: In 'Who's Gonna Take the Weight?' (Luke Cage S1#3) Colon visits Harlem's Paradise, accuses Cottonmouth of breaking his word on the Hammer gun sale from S1#1, demands a refund or the guns and threatens war when refused. changes.evidence: Turk is a Hell's Kitchen crook who is only visiting Harlem in 'Code of the Streets' (Luke Cage S1#2), playing chess at Pop's; after seeing Cottonmouth throw Tone off the roof he says he is going back to Hell's Kitchen. 'Harlem hustler' is wrong.

proposed.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S5#22
proposed.text: The dying Coulson refuses the serum that could save him and hides it in Daisy's gauntlets so she can stop Talbot. He then says goodbye and leaves to spend his last days in Tahiti.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: Daisy's recruiter and father figure. Gives up his cure so she can win, then says goodbye.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: Coulson's recruit and like a daughter to him. He gives up his cure so she can stop Talbot.

changes.evidence: In 'The End' (Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S5#22) Coulson refuses the Centipede serum and secretly hides it in Daisy's gauntlets while convincing her to face Talbot; she uses it to defeat him. Coulson then bids the agents farewell and leaves with May to spend his last days in Tahiti. The connection has only its S1 stage.

proposed.title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S4#22
proposed.text: Enoch leads a squad into a diner, freezes Daisy and the rest of Coulson's team in stasis and takes them away.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: A stranger who freezes Daisy's team in a diner and takes them away.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: One of the agents Enoch freezes in a diner and takes away.

changes.evidence: In the closing scene of 'World's End' (Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S4#22) Enoch's men burst into Rae's Restaurant and Enoch freezes Coulson's team, Daisy included, then takes them away; in S5#1 he sends them to 2091. The connection starts here, not in S5. Kind: this is how S4#22 leaves them (abducted by a stranger); the owner may prefer ally.

proposed.text: In the past, Daisy spends time with a younger Jiaying without telling her that she is her daughter. Nathaniel Malick reveals the truth to Jiaying just before he kills her.
proposed.on_a_card_about_b: Daisy's mother. Daisy meets her younger self in the past, before Nathaniel kills her.
proposed.on_b_card_about_a: Jiaying's daughter, who meets her younger self in the past without saying who she is.

changes.evidence: In 'After, Before' (S7#8) Daisy sends the team to Afterlife for her mother's help, and in 'Stolen' (Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S7#10) S.H.I.E.L.D. keeps Jiaying at the Lighthouse, Daisy spends time with her without revealing she is her daughter, and Nathaniel tells Jiaying the truth before killing her. The stages end at S2#22.

now.title: Daredevil: Born Again S2#8
now.text: BB reveals that Fisk's people murdered Blake, and the truth helps turn the city against Fisk.
now.on_a_card_about_b: Blake's old boss, whose people murder him.
now.on_b_card_about_a: Fisk's former aide, murdered by his people. The truth about it turns the city against Fisk.

changes.evidence: Blake is dead by 'The Southern Cross' (Daredevil: Born Again S2#8) and appears only in a photo and mentions. The stage is BB revealing the murder in her broadcast: a third person acting after his death, not something between Blake and Fisk. The murder itself is already stage 3 (S2#7).

owner_calls.question: The two never share a title. In 'The Writing on the Wall' (Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S2#7) Skye only mentions a source called Micro, who is never seen. Is that Micro on screen the same man as The Punisher's David Lieberman?
options: Keep: an off-screen tie stated on screen (fan wikis treat the two as one character)
Drop: nothing on screen links the AoS Micro to Lieberman, so the shared nickname is the only connection
owner_calls.evidence: Skye: 'One of my sources, this guy, Micro, he's kind of a crime scene junkie.' He is mentioned only, never shown. The fandom wiki merges him with Lieberman and calls Lieberman a Rising Tide member, citing only that AoS episode; The Punisher never links Lieberman to the Rising Tide or to Skye.
